## Editorial pass 2026-08-29

No assignment yet, and this may be the keystone article on the board. Four notes.

**1. The title names the example; the idea has a better one.** "Make the world into source a runtime can reject" is the whole of everything-as-code in eight words, and it is already sitting in the pitch. That is the title candidate and the opening line. "DeckBot as everything-as-code example" describes a work order, not an article.

**2. This is probably the keystone, and it should ship early.** "Source a runtime can reject" is the premise underneath at least three other stories:
- f10464 hill-climbing works because something can score and reject a version
- 864e95 Kanbus works because issues are a schema a validator can reject
- 4f3e30 the wiki piece works because a dumb checker can reject a bad page

If this ships first, all three can link it instead of re-explaining it. It currently has the least planning done of any story here. Worth reconsidering the order.

**3. The rewrite will fight itself.** DeckBot was the *point* of the Nov 2025 article and is now demoted to one example. A rewrite that keeps the old scaffolding will keep arguing the old thesis underneath the new one. Recommend writing the new spine cold — Marp/slides, Terraform, Playwright as three instances of the same move — and dropping DeckBot in as one of them, rather than editing the existing draft top to bottom. Decide this before anyone opens the file.

**4. Write the assignment first.** The idea says "needs rewrite, not a proofread," but nobody has written down what the new spine is. That is the actual next step, not copywriting.

**Research: none needed.** Needs an assignment and a rewrite-vs-restart decision.

comments.text:
## Rewrite delivered 2026-08-29 — for Sol's review

Full rewrite of `Anth.us/src/blog/everything-as-code-integration.mdx`. **Uncommitted on `develop`** so the diff is reviewable: 111 insertions, 194 deletions, 1,885 -> 1,807 words. MDX compiles (verified against `@mdx-js/mdx` + `remark-gfm`).

### First: the article was already public

`state: draft` does not gate publication. `gatsby-node.js` `createPages` builds a page for every MDX under `src/blog` with no state filter; only the homepage listings filter on `state: { eq: "published" }`. The old draft has been live and crawlable at https://anth.us/blog/everything-as-code-integration/ — unlisted, wearing a DRAFT banner, with three literal `[Diagram of...]` placeholder boxes visible on the page. Worth knowing as a general repo hazard, not just for this story.

### What changed and why

**Title.** "DeckBot: AI presentation assistant" -> "Everything as Code: Source a Runtime Can Reject". Title, slug, and body previously disagreed about the subject; the slug was already right, so it is unchanged and inbound links survive. Date held at 2025-11-30 per Ryan.

**New spine: the rejecter.** The old draft said "validate" a dozen times without landing why it matters. The thesis is now explicit and load-bearing: the value is not that a model can read your system, it is that something can *refuse* what the model writes before it lands. Rejection is the reason the pattern works, not a safety feature bolted on.

**Opens on `/proc`.** Best asset in the old draft, previously buried two-thirds down. Now the lede — kernel state rendered as text so every existing tool works on it.

**Three instances of one move**, as a table: Terraform/HCL/`plan`, Playwright/spec/test run, Marp/Markdown/compiler. DeckBot demoted from the frame to the worked version of the third.

**Replaced a placeholder with real evidence.** The promised before/after now exists: an actual AWS `describe-security-groups` JSON blob against the equivalent Terraform resource. Crucially the section argues *against* the token-compression framing — `"protocol": "tpc"` is accepted by the API and becomes a downstream incident; `protocol = "tpc"` is refused by `terraform validate`. Same typo, two failure modes. That is the point; brevity is the smaller prize.

**Fixed a false claim.** The old draft asserted DSLs "make hallucinations impossible by construction." That is wrong and would have been dunked on. It is now a named failure mode, "Confusing valid with correct": a grammar constrains form, not truth — valid HCL can reference a nonexistent subnet, flawless SQL can hit a renamed table.

**DeckBot section rewritten from scratch.** The old one was pasted README (Features bullets, BDD subsection). BDD is kept but repurposed: a `.feature` file is source and `behave` is its rejecter, which is the article's own thesis applied to the project's behavior. The NotebookLM contrast survived because it is a real argument about editability.

**"Anthus OS" -> "The Anthus Platform"** (3 occurrences, previously inconsistent), per Ryan.

**Cut:** all three placeholder boxes (the `placeholder-box` CSS class was used by no other article), both pure-noun filler lists, the anaphora block, the seven-item bolded virtue list, and the "This is not configuration / This is cognitive infrastructure" ending. Ends on "Build the rejecter first."

**Added a fifth failure mode** — "assuming validation is free" — because the rejecter is the actual deliverable and underfunding it is the most common way this pattern fails in practice.

### Open questions for Sol

1. **Hero image.** The only assets are DeckBot-branded. A DeckBot hero on an article that just demoted DeckBot re-creates the confusion we removed, so the piece now opens on the `/proc` code block and the hero moved into the DeckBot section. This breaks the house pattern of a centered image at top. Deliberate, and reversible — but a purpose-made hero would be better than either option. `preview_image` still points at the DeckBot asset for social cards.
2. **Backdating exposure.** Held at 2025-11-30, so nothing post-dating that is referenced. Sol should sanity-check that the Terraform/Playwright/Marp/Nano Banana claims are all defensible as of Nov 2025.
3. **`state` is still `draft`.** Deliberately not flipped — going live is Ryan's call plus a merge to `main`, not something to do inside a rewrite.
4. Nano Banana is linked to the Imagen page; the old draft said "Nano Banana Pro 2" in one place and "Nano Banana (Google Imagen)" in another. Worth a naming check.
